items.t: Townhomes cluster on the Sardis side (Vedder, Stevenson and Promontory Roads) plus smaller infill in Chilliwack Proper (Broadway Street, Yale Road).
Sardis stock sits in Schedule B5 of the 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP); north-side stock in Schedule B2.
City-wide facts: see chilliwack-houses-for-sale.
Townhomes are strata in the R4 (Low Density Multi-Unit Residential) Zone: minimum site 1,200 square metres, width 30 metres.
Garrison Crossing's CD-9 Zone sets townhouses to R4 standards; rowhouses: minimum lot 170 square metres.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Rentals and pets are set by each strata's filed bylaws, not by the City; the Province directs buyers to the Form B.
Buildings need a form and character permit in Development Permit Area 8 (Residential), per the City's December 2025 guide.
Sardis sites sit on the Vedder River fan, covered by an OCP permit area, so flood design forms part of approvals.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Sardis Park, 6898 School Lane: 5-hectare former gravel pit, pond, 655-metre loop trail, behind the Stevenson Road cluster.
Watson Glen Park, Tyson Road at Cumberland Avenue: 11.12 hectares; its fill built the Vedder Road Cottonwood overpass.
Sardis Sports Complex, 5725 Tyson Road: three rinks; Sardis Library: 5819 Tyson Road.
Promontory complexes are in a Wildlife Issue Area: no carts at the curb before 5:00 a.m. on collection day.
Wildlife Issue Area complexes must use wildlife-resistant carts, per the City's solid waste page.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Small-scale multi-unit development, 9119 Broadway Street: permit DP001883, Development Permit Area 6 (Infill), reviewed by the Design Review Advisory Committee June 10, 2025. Status: design review (as of November 3, 2026); developer and count not stated.
Sardis projects: see sardis-townhomes-for-sale. City pipeline: see chilliwack-houses-for-sale.
Strata fees and levies are set by each strata corporation; no official page states a fee for any Chilliwack complex.
A rented townhome still sits in a Speculation and Vacancy Tax area, because the Province lists Chilliwack as taxable; the owner declares annually.
Route 51 Vedder links Stevenson clusters to Downtown Chilliwack and the University of the Fraser Valley campus.
Route 54 Promontory serves Promontory rowhouses via Vedder Road and Teskey Way, to Cottonwood Mall.
Route 58 Tyson serves south Sardis from Cottonwood Mall, via Keith Wilson Road and Watson Road.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Sardis sites: check the Vedder fan permit area and Bylaw No. 4519, 75-metre Vedder River setback.
Promontory sites: Development Permit Area 2 hillside rules require a geotechnical report.
Read the depreciation report and Form B for fees, levies and reserve health, per strata guidance.

faq.a: Treat them as strata unless title documents say otherwise. R4 and CD-9 townhome development is built as strata complexes, so provincial strata guidance on bylaws, fees and levies applies. The legal check is the strata plan and Form B for the specific complex, which show its rental and age bylaws.
faq.q: Are Chilliwack townhomes strata or freehold?

faq.a: On the Sardis side: the Villas at Sardis Park at 45819 Stevenson Road, Iron Horse rowhomes at 46211 Promontory Road, and Garrison Crossing forms under CD-9, all named on City or developer records. North of the river, supply is smaller infill, such as 9119 Broadway Street.

Only if the strata's bylaws allow it. Provincial guidance states strata corporations set rental bylaws, summarized in the unit's Form B, so ask for current bylaws before offering. Purpose-built rentals differ: at York Residences, Campus Drive, the operator sets terms itself and states pets are not allowed.
faq.q: Can I rent out a townhome?

faq.a: At building stage, yes. 4519 sets a 75-metre setback from the Vedder River and floors at flood construction level plus 0.6 metres. For existing complexes, check the depreciation report and strata insurance.
